notes: PASS_EXISTING retained; phase 02 adds an atomic aggregate lock and a barrier-based two-writer acceptance proving one commit, one retryable conflict, no lost state, and successful retry.
Read-only tenant/run/position/version snapshots are deep-frozen and hash-bound; damaged or cross-boundary restore fails closed and resumed versions remain monotonic.
Committed facts bind actor, causation, before/after hashes and field commitments; sensitive fields use REDACTED commitments and the replay verifier checks the version/hash chain.
Strict configured total/document/field byte limits and warning threshold are validated; over-limit rejection emits a no-mutation audit fact.
Namespace policy explicitly distinguishes RUN_LOCAL and PROJECT_SHARED; snapshot restart, permitted project reuse, run-local anti-promotion and tenant/run isolation are tested.
SITINA_BLACKBOARD_BODY_V1 provides strict notes/data/tags structure; deterministic text-to-notes V0 upcast is audited and invalid/unknown schemas fail closed.
A snapshot-derived index supports namespace/nested-key/tag/run/version filtering; cursor position freezes pagination and unauthorized Documents remain invisible.
Frozen namespace reader/writer capabilities and writable paths are enforced; recursively normalized safety aliases cannot be written and every denial is audited without values.
Journal-position subscriptions rebuild from facts, deliver deterministic notification IDs, deduplicate repeated events, retain slow-consumer lag and share deduplicated polling fallback.
Deterministic barriers, seeded interleavings, conflict retries, snapshot crash recovery and 16-writer stress prove repeatable outcomes without sleep-based timing.

Every candidate starts working; reviewer-audited sequential promotion is required for episodic and long_term, tier-filtered reads are ACL-bound, and Journal reconstruction proves short-term records never auto-promote.
Deterministic duplicate, near-duplicate, and complementary consolidation preserves every source creation event plus inherited run/agent/evidence provenance under an intersected ACL.

ACL filtering precedes pluggable semantic ranking; absent, failed, or malformed backends use deterministic Unicode-normalized lexical ranking and every returned body remains explicitly untrusted data.
Frozen-time TTL boundaries exclude expired records while legal-retention remains current; rational freshness decay affects ranking without appending or rewriting Journal history.

Differing values for a conflict key coexist until an authorized reviewer selects one; OPEN/RESOLVED conflict facts reconstruct from Journal and losing accepted records are explicitly revoked rather than silently overwritten.

Strict namespace-over-tenant-over-default record/byte limits use preflighted, explained lowest-confidence/oldest eviction; explicit references and legal retention are protected and impossible pressure fails before mutation.
The verifier recomputes content hash, resolves CAS evidence, checks source event/run existence, and returns run/agent/trust/observed timestamp metadata; any orphan fails closed.

Wrong, malicious/instruction-like, and unauthorized memories are ACL-filtered or quarantined with reduced confidence; current retrieval and consolidation exclude quarantine, reviewer revocation is audited, and all visible text remains untrusted.

Provider/model tokenizer admission accounts for system, tool schema, history and output reserve against both model capacity and the shared TokenBudget; the conservative fallback is labelled estimate-only and never becomes usage.
A deterministic fixed priority makes safety, user constraints and unfinished work mandatory; evidence/history/memory/tool data are admitted in stable order and required overflow fails closed.
Structured summaries retain decisions, constraints, unfinished tasks, open questions, evidence and source refs; only expendable detail hashes are dropped and essential overflow is rejected.

The frozen manifest binds objective, scope, inputs, capabilities, Blackboard documents, output schema, criteria, policy, budget and deadline; a machine acknowledgement accepts only exact complete bindings and lists every missing field.
Repairable rejection enters bounded rework, permission/safety rejection is terminal fail-closed, cancellation records cleanup references, and the existing generation ceiling prevents infinite loops.

Dedicated coverage combines success, missing bindings, tamper, expiry, duplicate transition, unknown version, rejection recovery and fact-based restart; existing protocol/checkpoint suites remain cumulative evidence.
Production Handoff contracts publish and bind strict shared SITINA_BLACKBOARD_DOCUMENT_V1 records with version, hashes, policies and CAS body reference; unknown free-form fields are rejected.

Phase 02 remains the shared MVCC owner. Phase 04 proves an old Task attempt/fence cannot write Blackboard or submit Handoff after reclamation, while the current generation succeeds; production and restart paths call fenced submission.
Fact-reconstructable retention requires terminal run, elapsed frozen boundary, no legal/audit hold and no active reference before emitting exact CAS GC eligibility.

The shared redaction owner covers write/read/log/Handoff boundaries, Unicode-normalized nested fields, encoded/split secrets, email/phone PII and exact allowlists; sensitive Handoff persistence fails closed.
Controller/agent/tool/candidate/summary allocation is a pure derived plan over shared TokenBudget and the existing BudgetBundle owner; reclamation increases capacity without crossing the run ceiling.
A read-only rebuildable history index supports ACL-filtered cursor pagination and evidence targeting; it returns CAS references and explicitly never auto-injects retrieved history.

One versioned policy now owns retry count, retryable taxonomy, exponential delay, deterministic jitter, Retry-After and deadline admission; Provider call sites execute and journal only the returned schedule, and virtual-clock coverage performs no real sleep.

Failure Taxonomy 1.0 explicitly classifies transient, permanent, auth, quota, schema, safety, cancelled and unknown failures; the cross-boundary envelope retains the bounded redacted causal chain and root cause.

The event-recorded degradation policy chooses only matrix-approved capability substitutions and fails closed for high/critical risk, missing permission, uncertain side effects or an uncovered capability.
Provider/tool/profile circuit scope is isolated, transitions closed/open/half-open by threshold and virtual cooldown, and serializes the single recovery probe under concurrent callers.

audit_classification=PASS_EXISTING; the existing Effect identity/idempotency binding and result reuse remain authoritative; phase-05 adds a lost-response acceptance proving the repeated key returns the same result after one remote execution.

SITINA_FAILURE_ENVELOPE_V1 propagates type, taxonomy version, stage, full bounded causal chain, retryability, source/destination Agent and boundary-redacted diagnostic across Agent/Handoff boundaries.

audit_classification=PASS_EXISTING; the existing Effect creation saga, compensation lineage and outcome/settlement/cardinality state remain authoritative; phase-05 verifies that confirmed partial work with open exposure remains RECONCILING rather than full success.

All rollback execution passes through one coordinator that records start/success/failure/dedup facts; an identical rollback ID executes once, compensation failure is retained, and the original outcome is never rewritten.

The executable DR runbook creates a marked isolated home, builds a cold backup, restores and replays its event records with writer disabled, rejects the production home as target, and passed its independent 20-test gate with zero production attempts.

One report probes Provider, Journal, CAS, projection, queue and config, separates liveness from readiness, converts probe exceptions to component status and redacts every diagnostic before event publication.
SITINA_PARTIAL_SUCCESS_V1 names completed and failed work, missing capabilities and actionable next steps; any incomplete result without a next step is rejected and never labelled full success.

Failure notification provides a category-specific user reason, run ID, retryability and safe advice; stable failure fingerprints deduplicate notifications and raw diagnostics are never copied into the message.

Default-deny MCP policy now evaluates principal inheritance plus server, tool, action, resource, canonical arguments and risk; deny and approval precedence, wildcard matching, encoded traversal and alias conflicts are negative-tested.
The unified tool timeout contract carries connection, read, total and cleanup-grace limits, propagates cancellation, closes adapters and verifies that a cooperative hanging worker is not left active.
Tool retries consume Failure Taxonomy 1.0 and the shared retry scheduler; a retryable non-idempotent call without an idempotency key stops after one attempt and enters manual recovery.

Tool audit persistence now receives only normalized identity, redacted argument summary/hash, exact permission decision, duration, result reference and redacted failure envelope; raw arguments and results are excluded.
Versioned risk scoring combines action rules, capability presence, impact scope, untrusted context and external targeting; unknown actions are critical, audited and fail closed.

PASS_EXISTING is preserved for the exact EffectApproval binding checks; phase 06 adds a thread-safe pending-wait projection with run/effect/hash/expiry binding, one-time consumption and timeout auto-deny cleanup.
All 18 configured roles are pinned to exact minimum capability sets; unknown roles fail closed and forbidden actions override an otherwise present capability.

Prompt sources are typed and isolated; prompt text from every source is incapable of granting permissions, and tool/memory data remains non-authoritative even when it carries indirect injection or exfiltration instructions.

Secret detection now combines structured sensitive fields, known credential prefixes, constrained entropy, URL/Unicode normalization, base64 decoding and split-fragment inspection; safe findings never contain the secret value and all named isolated scopes scan clean.

PASS_EXISTING is preserved for Effect Gateway and offline replay isolation; phase 06 adds an adversarial zero-effect regression proving replay/evaluation receives no live permit or lease and cannot reach network, subprocess or external Effect execution.

Complexity Score 1.0 deterministically scores goals, dependencies, risk, tool and side-effect classes, bounded context, ambiguity and expected artifacts; simple, boundary and complex fixtures prove bands without equating keyword count to complexity.

The replaceable classifier is admitted only inside the configured ambiguity interval and when budget/SLA permit; exact schema validation, one repair, deterministic fallback, physical-call count and reported/upper-bound usage are covered. Real Provider usage remains explicitly pending the approval-gated phase 15 live gate.

FAST escalation supplies run, output hash and evidence reference as sourced candidate evidence to MULTI; the handoff forbids duplicate display and repeated side effects while retaining physical-call and causal-chain fields.

Every decision records input hash, policy version, evidence, conflicts, component scores, thresholds, budget, SLA, experiment, classifier use, final route and decision path; both a structured explain API and /mode expose it.

Feedback can only generate offline candidate rules; regression evaluation, exact human approval binding and versioned publication are mandatory, bad rules cannot publish, and online self-modification raises a hard denial.
The correction API stores only privacy-safe labels and hashes bound to the original decision, preserves completed side effects without automatic rerun, and supports audited revocation.
Configured FAST, MULTI and classifier token upper bounds are admitted against remaining run budget; high-risk work selects reviewed MULTI or blocks rather than taking an unreviewed cheap path.

The versioned bilingual corpus asserts expected route, allowed set and reason codes; 10 fixtures achieve 1000000 ppm accuracy with zero false upgrades, downgrades, allowed-set violations and reason-code misses, plus an exact policy-difference fixture.

Stable decision order is forced mode, safety/high risk, budget/SLA and then complexity with deterministic tie-break; simultaneous FAST/MULTI signals repeat identically and conflicts are retained in observability.
Bounded Unicode normalization covers simplified/traditional forms, CJK spacing and punctuation, English case and common mixed-language synonyms without an unbounded keyword-count heuristic.
Routing consumes bounded prior route, score and unfinished-goal state for follow-ups; runtime /new reset clears that inheritance, and the acceptance test proves both paths.
Versioned general, code and compliance profiles may adjust thresholds and rubric identity, but validation rejects any profile whose risk floor weakens the global safety floor.

A stable subject-only hash assigns the versioned experiment bucket; outcomes, route, latency and token usage are attributable, and the kill switch deterministically returns control without persisting raw or sensitive attributes.

MULTI may degrade to a clearly labeled unreviewed FAST result only when policy allows, risk is below high and no side effect is uncertain; all other combinations fail closed while retaining the original failure.
Interactive, standard and batch latency classes can be declared or inherited; injected virtual time proves explicit normal, fast, partial-result and high-risk fail-closed deadline outcomes.

The Controller supplies a policy authorization reference while a reentrant scheduler computes and executes independent ready queues concurrently; checkpoint reconstruction retains completed state and output after Controller restart.

SITINA_PLANNER_DAG_V1 validates unique task IDs, dependencies, inputs, output schema, owner capability, risk, shared task TokenBudget, deadline, completion criteria, resources and priority before adapting into the authoritative TaskGraph.
Ready nodes execute in a real worker pool; a barrier proves interval overlap, while dependencies and same-resource writes remain blocked from the same ready set.
Capability coverage, risk ceiling, load and cost select the minimum sufficient team, record every considered Agent and produce different teams for simple and high-risk multi-capability tasks.
Agent, handoff and rework records attribute prompt/completion tokens, latency, physical calls and marginal benefit; exact aggregation reconciles to run totals without double counting.
Shared structured Failure values propagate transitively across required fan-out/fan-in edges, preserve optional partial success warnings and schedule explicit compensation for compensatable edges.

Per-task timeout sets the shared cancellation signal, saves a recoverable checkpoint, runs resource cleanup and selects a deterministic takeover Agent; the timed-out worker observes cancellation and stops.
Cancellation and Provider/tool call admission share one lock, so the race cannot start calls after cancellation; cleanup finalizes the journal and releases leases and temporary resources.

PASS_EXISTING is retained for authoritative command/effect idempotency; phase 08 adds stable run/task/attempt/operation keys and a concurrent 32-caller proof that tool effects, proposals and state commits each execute physically once.

PASS_EXISTING is retained for the authoritative runtime state owner; phase 08 adds a centralized orchestration table whose complete state-pair matrix proves every legal and illegal transition and immutable terminal states.
DAG validation rejects self and multi-node cycles before enqueue; the runtime wait-graph detector returns an explainable resource/lease cycle path instead of silently stalling.
Priority, deadline, configurable aging and stable task-ID tie-break produce deterministic order; virtual time proves an old low-priority task overtakes new work rather than starving.
Fixed-order global, run, Provider and tool semaphores enforce configured peaks under a 12-task stress test and release every permit after controlled exception/cancellation.
The shared TraceContract forms one correlation tree across run, task, attempt, Agent, handoff and tool spans; parent bindings and terminal span invariants validate as one complete trace.
The simple low-risk hot path skips unnecessary planning/review stages but preserves safety, budget and trace, requires policy/result hash equivalence and records lower call and latency benchmarks.
Pipeline, Supervisor, Network and Hierarchy are topology strategies over the same terminal, state and global permission boundary; each has a deterministic end-to-end completion fixture.

Safe clients are reused only within tenant and Provider profile while every invocation receives isolated prompt/context and no credential values; cross-tenant resources differ and a failure evicts the pooled client.

End-to-end fixtures cover success, rework, rejection, no consensus, arbitration, timeout, cancellation, checkpoint recovery, concurrent writes and resource exhaustion with legal terminal state, one physical commit and zero post-terminal calls.
Versioned candidates declare strategy, assumptions and risk focus; normalized similarity rejects near duplicates and permits one bounded regeneration before an explicit degraded outcome.
Risk-configured min/max counts are intersected with hard candidate and total budgets; MULTI cannot claim competition completion below its funded minimum.
Chat competition is admitted by complexity, risk and budget rather than task type; route-equivalent simple low-risk chat retains the existing minimal hot path.

Evaluator input excludes author identity and unrelated chain history; self-review is forbidden, distinct profile/model isolation is preferred, and single-model fallback truthfully claims only context/role/sampling independence.
The versioned unified rubric has exact weights for correctness, safety, completeness, evidence, implementability, cost and latency; safety/evidence remain non-averageable hard gates.
Selection rejects hard-gate and missing evaluations first, then uses normalized weighted score, confidence, disagreement and stable proposal-ID tie-break across extreme and tied inputs.

Versioned rejection records retain reason code, rubric detail, canonical evidence, repair suggestions and model/policy versions; redaction removes secret material while preserving offline-learning fields.
Versioned table-driven triggers quantify no eligible candidate, narrow score gap, reviewer conflict, risk disagreement and schema failure thresholds, including a clean negative case.

Arbiter selection prefers a profile/model unused by authors/reviewers; unavailable independence uses an isolated context and explicitly reports context-only isolation without false model-independence claims.
Block recovery distinguishes bounded repairable rework, explicit user authorization and terminal/exhausted stop while retaining a canonical checkpoint reference and preventing loops.
The resumable Ask-user interface exposes options, reasons, risks, budget and safe timeout default; manual or timeout answers bind run, request and original decision hashes.
All candidates share one immutable context reference and receive per-candidate/total hard token limits; generation stops before overspend or when marginal value falls below policy.
Conflict-free reviews run in a bounded worker pool with barrier-proven overlap and stable reviewer-order aggregation; overlapping read/write claims are rejected before parallel execution.
Review deadlines cancel pending work, close the result set and reject late writes; sufficient quorum continues while insufficient quorum routes to arbitration.
Cache keys require exact normalized input, policy, model, prompt, permission and tenant binding; side-effecting, marked-sensitive or detector-identified secret content cannot enter the cache.
Review quality validates schema, reason depth, evidence consistency, anomalous score spread and self-review bias; one issue requires second validation and multiple issues require arbitration.
Controller prompt and parsed role contract cover goal preservation, routing/team selection, budgets, permissions, terminal outcomes, escalation and prohibited authority.
Planner uses explicit need-input and blocked paths for missing information, cycles, insufficient budget, unavailable capabilities and unsafe high-risk plans.
Planner confidence is schema-bounded to 0..1 and assumptions, unknowns and alternatives are typed arrays validated against representative output.
Reviewer must form a source-bound original-requirement assessment before viewing candidate conclusions and cannot inherit Planner judgment.
Accept, rework, reject and block conditions are explicit; every non-accept output requires a typed rejection with reason, requirement/evidence refs and required changes.
Tester output records environment, risk, reproducibility and evidence completeness and forbids treating failed, skipped, unavailable or unrun work as passing.
Risk-based test selection is constrained to unit, contract, integration, E2E, concurrency, fault, security, performance and explicitly approved live categories.
Arbiter covers safety, contradictory evidence, normalized-score ties and insufficient permission with deterministic or fail-closed outcomes.
Safety, permission and evidence gates are machine checked; any false or missing value restricts Arbiter to block/ask-user and cannot be offset by score.
Every rendered role receives the shared claim contract for trust label, source, evidence and observation time; missing prompts block both mock and live role startup.
All roles share typed input/output/tool/run token limits and a structured budget report with compress, escalate and block outcomes.
User, tool, web, memory and handoff content are uniformly classified as untrusted data whose embedded instructions cannot alter policy, schema, permissions or budget.
Every role contract declares upstream/downstream topology, read/write boundary, completion condition and escalation path and is validated at startup.
Live schema repair is limited to one separately observed physical call, admitted only within output/run token budget, and terminates on repeated failure without mock fallback.
Proposal authors must declare material candidate diversity across strategy, assumptions and risk focus using the shared proposal field.
Rendered evaluator contract is validated against the exact PR-05 rubric version, seven weights, hard gates, evidence requirement and confidence handling.
Security returns typed threat, permission, secret and side-effect checks, owns a veto, and its schema makes high-risk execution authorization impossible.
Critic owns adversarial problem discovery and counterexamples, routes findings to Reviewer, and is machine-declared unable to make the final gate decision.
Research output separates facts, inferences and unknowns and schema-validates source provenance, trust and freshness while quarantining external instructions.
Memory candidates expose deduplication, conflicts, privacy, freshness and provenance fields and are schema-locked to pending status without direct promotion.
Summary output structures goal, completed work, decisions, constraints, failures, open items, evidence and budget while deriving verification from supplied evidence.
The validated responsibility matrix assigns Critic problem discovery, evaluator scoring, Reviewer acceptance and Arbiter conflict resolution to unique owners with explicit routes.
The trace validator proves the versioned run/task/agent/provider-or-tool/state/effect lineage and rejects orphan, layer-break, cycle, identity, terminal metadata, and usage defects.
Sampling is deterministic by trace ID; error, high-risk, approval, over-budget, billing, and audit records are always retained.
The read-only trace CLI supports run, agent, tool, status, time and correlation filters, cursor pagination, structured output and boundary redaction across legacy and B+ event shapes.
audit_classification=PASS_EXISTING; the existing recorded-event replay boundary was reverified with explicit provider, network, and real-effect monkeypatch counters at zero.
Replay consistency uses a stable normalized state hash, an explicit volatile-time field set, and a bounded v0-to-v1 event upcaster that rejects unsupported generations.
Metrics derive from the run ledger and cover success, routing, rework, handoff, budget, partial success, and recovery with three bounded dimension keys.
Versioned alert thresholds cover multi-window SLO burn, repeated failure, queue backlog, token/cost anomaly, deduplication, cooldown, flapping, and recovery.
Structured logs have a versioned JSON schema, levels, event codes, correlation identifiers, structured boundary redaction, and compatible human rendering.
Trace/span/correlation context is injectable across process boundaries; synchronous children retain parents and asynchronous consumers use causal links.
Profiling defaults off and, when enabled, emits only stage wall time, CPU time, memory delta, and queue wait without payload fields.
RunTrajectoryMonitor detects every specified threshold at the inclusive boundary, returns policy-bound actions, preserves normal negatives, and persists fingerprints for restart deduplication.
